messages.author: 68d0ddf2537ec510
messages.subject: Interpretation of stepwiseQTL
parts:
Dear Dr. Broman,

 

I have questions considering the interpretation of stepwiseqtl and would be very obliged if you could help me.

If I identify additional QTL in stepwise, I would like to judge how far those are above the detection threshold and if they depend on the interaction with another QTL (would I need to run e.g. “addpair” afterwards?). In your book you write that the threshold can be determined by summary.scantwoperm; which thresholds would you use to determine significance of an additional QTL (LODav1?), and how could I distinguish a QTL-interaction (additive/epistatic)?

What does the column “one” represent in the summary.scantwoperm?

Is there a way to extract the main LOD-score peaks and p-values for the output of stepwiseqtl (comparable to summary.scanone)?

 

Kind regards,


Jasper

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpretation of stepwiseQTL
parts:
The output of stepwiseqtl() is a qtl object. You can use it in fitqtl() to fit the specific model and get the drop-one-QTL-at-a-time table which would give you information about the strength of evidence of the individual QTL. The output of stepwiseqtl() should also include a formula which indicates which QTL are involved in interactions. You would want to provide that formula to fitqtl() so that you're consider the selected model and not the strictly additive one.

The system for selecting multiple-QTL models including interactions is described in Chapter 9 of the R/qtl book; also see Manichaikul et al (2009), https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.108.094565 The way in which the thresholds are turned into penalties is somewhat complicated.

The "one" column in the scantwoperm output is for the single-QTL model; it should correspond to what you get if you did a permutation test with scanone().

karl

Dear Karl,

Thanks for your quick reply!
I was wondering, when interpreting the strength of the evidence of the individual QTLs using the fitqtl() method, is there then also a way to get a significance threshold to help interpret the LOD scores of the drop-one-QTL-at-a-time table? As these QTLs are part of a multiple-QTL model, I assume the permutations from scanone() or the "one" column are not appropriate here? Similarly, for any interactions in the drop-one-QTL table, should I use a different threshold than for the individual QTLs in the drop-one-QTL table?

Best Wishes,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpretation of stepwiseQTL
parts:
If there are no interactions to be considered, then you can use the scanone permutation threshold to gauge the value of those individual QTL's LOD scores.

Interactions are more complicated if you're using the "light" and "heavy" interaction penalties. But you're pretty much comparing them to one or the other of those.

For QTL that are involved in an interaction, dropping the QTL involves dropping the interaction as well, so you'd look at the main-effect penalty plus a light or heavy interaction penalty.

What you want to think about are the different multiple-QTL models and try to derive the penalized LOD scores for them, with preference to the model with largest penalized LOD score.

Note that if you adjust the stringency of the penalties, the relative value of different models will change.

karl
